- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 1–2%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model often undercorrects; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model tends to overpredict early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed; apply 0.5–1.5% downward bias for first 5–7 days.
- Mean reversion is stronger in 10–15 day horizon; if forecast deviates >2% from 10-day moving average, adjust toward it with 0.5–1.0% smoothing.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model often misjudges direction; align forecast with sentiment pivot point, not trend continuation.
